question: BPL is an economic benchmark related to threshold income. What does "BPL" stand for?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Below Poverty Line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Below Poverty Line (BPL):-**

 
 
• It is a benchmark used by the government of India** to indicate economic disadvantage and to identify individuals and households in need of government assistance and aid.**
 
• It is determined using various parameters which vary from state to state and within states.
 
• The BPL benchmark is used by the government **to target various social welfare programs and schemes to the poorest and most vulnerable sections of society.**
 
• The BPL concept is also used by various non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and other charitable institutions to identify and target their poverty alleviation and development programs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Base Price Line:-**

 
 
• **It is a pricing strategy that involves setting different prices for products within a product line, based on their perceived value or quality. **
 
• The goal of base price lining is to maximize profits by offering customers a range of choices at different price points, while still maintaining a consistent brand image.
 
 
 
• **Below Price Line:-**
 
 
• **It is a term used to describe products that are priced below the average market price for similar products.**
 
• This can be done for a variety of reasons, such as to attract new customers, to increase sales volume, or to clear out inventory.
